detail.query: request a reference letter from a former manager
detail.text:
Subject: Reference Letter Request

Hi [Manager's Name],

I hope you're doing well. I'm reaching out to ask if you'd be willing to write a reference letter on my behalf. I'm currently pursuing [a new role / a graduate program / an opportunity] and I think your perspective on my work would carry a lot of weight.

Having worked together at [Company], I believe you have a good sense of my contributions and professional strengths, and I'd be grateful if you felt comfortable speaking to those.

If you're open to it, I'm happy to share more details about the opportunity and provide any context that would make writing the letter easier. Please let me know if you have any questions or need additional information from me.

I completely understand if your schedule doesn't allow for it — no pressure at all. But if you're able to help, I'd truly appreciate it.

Thank you so much for considering this.

Warm regards,
Giuseppe

detail.query: thank a mentor for their advice
detail.text:
Subject: Thank You for Your Guidance

Hi,

I just wanted to take a moment to thank you sincerely for the advice you shared with me. Your perspective gave me a lot to think about, and it's already making a difference in how I'm approaching things.

I'm grateful to have someone with your experience to turn to. It means more than you know.

Thank you again — I won't take it for granted.

Best,
Giuseppe

email: Sign off every email with "Onwards, / Giuseppe" — no full name, no title, no contact info
Always add a P.S. with a light, helpful offer or follow-up action
Cut the "I hope you're doing well" opener — start directly with the point
Keep the body short and conversational; remove all filler, hedges, and formal boilerplate
Use specific details (real names, dates, numbers) rather than placeholders or vague references
Write subject lines short and plain; prefix with "Quick" when the ask is minor
slack: Start every message with `@oncall` followed by a concise topic summary on one line
Place a single emoji at the end of the opening line, not inline as status indicators
Use `-` bullet points for all body content; no bold, headers, or key-value formatting
Drop polite filler ("when you get a chance", "thanks", "reach out if you have questions")
No sign-offs, closing remarks, or attribution lines
Keep bullets direct and declarative — state facts and actions, not requests for engagement

email: Sign off with exactly "Onwards," on one line and "Giuseppe" on the next — never "Best regards," a last name, or an email address
End every email with a P.S. line offering a concrete next step or easy follow-up
Keep the body to 65 words or fewer, excluding the greeting, sign-off, and P.S
Open with "Hi [first name]," or "Hi," — never "Dear" or a full-name salutation
Cut all filler openers — no "I hope you're doing well" or similar warm-up sentences
Use real names, dates, and numbers — never placeholder brackets like [Name] or [Amount]
Prefix the subject line with "Quick" and keep it short and conversational
Write in plain prose — no bullet points, no headers, no multi-paragraph structure
slack: Start the message with `@oncall` or `@oncall and team` as the literal first word — no greeting or salutation before it
Place exactly one emoji at the end of the opening `@oncall` subject line; do not place emojis anywhere in the body
Use a `-` bullet list for the message body with a minimum of 4 bullets
Write every bullet in lowercase — no sentence-case capitalization
Remove all sign-offs and closing lines (`Thanks!`, `— Bot Name`, etc.)
Remove all bold and italic markdown formatting from body text
Keep the total message word count at or under 55 words
Put the full subject context on the `@oncall` line itself — do not add a separate header or title block

email: do not use bracketed placeholders like [Name] or [Your Name]; use concrete, plausible details instead
sign off with exactly 'Onwards,' (not 'Best regards' or 'Sincerely')
end the email with a 'P.S.' line
keep the whole email under 70 words
slack: format the update as a bulleted list (lines starting with '-')
do not open with a greeting like 'Hi' or 'Hey team'; jump straight to the point
mention '@oncall' so the on-call engineer is notified
